questions.q: What is the first step in turning a requirement into a data model, per this lesson?
options: Writing Apex classes for each object
Creating page layouts
Assigning user profiles
Listing every noun in the requirement as a candidate object
questions.explain: Listing the nouns (Claim, Asset, Product, Customer) is the starting point before any object gets built.

questions.q: In the warranty-claims model, why are Account and Asset NOT built as custom objects?
options: They already exist as standard Salesforce objects — the reuse-first principle applies
They can't be customized
Custom objects can't relate to each other
There was no time to build them
questions.explain: Account and Asset are standard objects already in the org, so they're reused rather than rebuilt as custom objects.

questions.q: What relationship shape should you use when one Asset can have many Warranty Claims, but each Claim belongs to exactly one Asset?
options: Many-to-many via a junction object
One-to-many (a lookup or master-detail field)
No relationship is needed
A formula field
questions.explain: A record that always belongs to exactly one parent is a one-to-many relationship, built with a lookup or master-detail field.

questions.q: Why does the warranty-claims model need Claim_Line_Item__c as a junction object?
options: Junction objects are required by Salesforce for every custom object
To improve page load speed
Because a single lookup field can't represent a many-to-many relationship between Claims and Products
Because Account and Asset can't be related directly
questions.explain: A many-to-many relationship (a Claim covering several Products, a Product appearing on many Claims) needs a junction object with two relationships, not a single field.

questions.q: What happens if a many-to-many relationship gets modeled as a simple one-to-many lookup instead?
options: The data literally can't be captured without duplicating records once both sides need multiple links
Nothing — the two shapes are interchangeable
The object becomes read-only
Reports stop working entirely
questions.explain: A simple lookup can't represent both-sides-multiple relationships — you hit a wall (and likely duplicate data) the first time the real-world data needs that shape.
